title: Trajectory hint strip for new workspaces
creator: Lina Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, dismissible horizontal 'trajectory hint strip' that appears at the top of newly created workspaces. The strip should orient new users to three high-impact first actions tailored to their org persona (Developer, Platform, Product): 1) create a sample endpoint / run a quick inference, 2) set a cost guardrail or view projected spend, 3) create a rollout (canary) with a template. The strip is a visual micro-journey: each step is a small card with an icon, a one-line CTA, and an inline micro-progress indicator. Variants: A (minimal static cards), B (animated ribbon with progressive affordance and inline preview), C (contextual variant that replaces a step when user has already completed one of the actions). Primary goals: reduce time-to-first-success, increase early activation of rollouts and cost controls, and teach where related dashboards live. Constraints: must be keyboard-accessible, not impact dashboard layout shift, trackable with analytics events, and dismissible persistently per-user. Avoid lengthy tutorial copy; prioritize action over explanation.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with three variants (A/B/C) delivered and linked
Animated interactions defined (hover, focus, dismiss) and exported as 3-second MP4s
Analytics event schema defined: trajectory_shown, step_clicked, step_completed, strip_dismissed
Engineering ticket created with layout spec and accessibility checklist
Usability test (5 users) shows median time-to-first-action <= 4 minutes for Variant B
Clear fallback behavior documented when workspace already has >1 project
comments: 2026-02-05 Lina Chen: Initial concept sketch uploaded. Focused on solving the 'where do I start' gap for new workspaces. Rough personas and three candidate CTAs included.
2026-02-09 Jonah Patel (Research): Ran 6 contextual interviews with Platform engineers. Key insight: users want a low-friction sample call and a one-click way to cap spend before exploring rollouts.
2026-02-11 Aisha Patel: Created high-fidelity cards in Figma. Variant B includes subtle progress pulses and an inline cost estimate micrograph. Shared with PM and Eng for early feedback.
2026-02-13 Marco Reyes (PM): Requested we add a 'snooze' state (30 days) in addition to persistent dismiss to reduce churn from accidental dismissals.

2026-02-14 Harper Lin (Eng): Flagged runtime layout concerns. If inserted above the main header, needs a non-jank CSS transition and metric on layout shift. Suggested injecting via portal to avoid huge reflows.

2026-02-16 Design review: Team preferred Variant B for discoverability but asked for a graceful minimal variant for low-contrast environments. Action: prepare accessibility color checks and motion-reduced experience.
2026-02-18 Usability test: 5 participants. Variant B beat A by 45% for median clicks to first successful inference. Participants noted the inline preview helped reduce uncertainty.

2026-02-19 Aisha Patel: Updated prototype with snooze option and 'already completed' state where a completed step shows a check and an alternate suggestion (e.g., explore rollouts -> configure canary percentage).
2026-02-20 Marco Reyes: Approved moving to handoff. PM requests tracking for conversion to 'create rollout' and 'set cost guardrail' within first 14 days.
2026-02-20 Harper Lin: Engineering acceptance criteria added to ENG-4021. POC for portal insertion and animation performance scheduled in sprint 18.
decisions: Ship Variant B (animated ribbon) as the default, with Variant A as a fallback for motion-reduced or low-performance contexts.
Persist dismiss and add 30-day snooze option to reduce accidental loss of education affordance.
Track three primary analytics events and wire them into growth + observability dashboards (conversion and time-to-action).
Design to hand off CSS animation guidance and a motion-reduced static state to Eng.
Prototype to include two copy lengths: concise and expanded for accessibility readers.
